items.text: Cluster nodes are built on certified Azure Local Premier Solutions or Integrated Systems
items.description: All physical servers must be validated and certified on the official Microsoft Azure Local Catalog (Integrated Systems or Premier Solutions from OEM partners like Dell, Lenovo, HPE) to guarantee driver/firmware compatibility and end-to-end support.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.azurestackhci/clusters' | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, properties.reportedProperties.clusterVersion

items.text: Cluster nodes have identical CPU, memory, and PCIe device configurations
items.description: Ensure hardware symmetry across all cluster nodes. Asymmetrical configurations (differing processor generations, varying memory capacities, or mismatched PCIe NIC slots) cause uneven resource scheduling, unpredictable failover behavior, and potential cluster instabilities.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.azurestackhci/edgedevices' | project id, name, properties

items.text: Host operating systems use dedicated boot storage controllers and mirrored drives
items.description: Operating system drives must use a dedicated controller (such as Dell BOSS-N1, Lenovo M.2 RAID, or SATADOM in RAID-1) physically isolated from the Storage Spaces Direct storage bus. OS drives must never reside on the same HBA/controller managing data pool drives.

items.text: TPM 2.0 and UEFI Secure Boot are enabled on all physical nodes
items.description: Verify in system BIOS/UEFI that TPM 2.0 (Trusted Platform Module) and Secure Boot are enabled and operational across all nodes to support Secured-core server capabilities, BitLocker volume encryption, and measured boot attestation.

items.text: Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) and Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI) are active
items.description: Ensure hardware virtualization extensions (VT-x / AMD-V, SLAT / EPT / NPT, and Intel VT-d / AMD-Vi IOMMU) are enabled in BIOS to support Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) and hypervisor-protected code integrity (HVCI), forming the foundation of Secured-core server.

items.text: Baseboard Management Controllers (BMC / IPMI) are isolated on a dedicated secure network
items.description: All node BMC interfaces (iDRAC, iLO, XCC) must be configured with static IP addresses on a dedicated out-of-band management VLAN. Default manufacturer passwords must be changed, TLS 1.3/1.2 enforced, and access restricted via management firewalls.

items.text: Cluster Quorum witness is configured using Azure Cloud Witness or a dedicated third-site File Share Witness
items.description: Every cluster must have an active quorum witness configured with Dynamic Quorum. For clusters with Internet access, use Azure Cloud Witness backed by an Azure Storage Account (TLS 1.2). For air-gapped or localized environments, configure a File Share Witness located outside the cluster's physical rack/fault domain.

items.text: Host memory and CPU capacity accounts for N+1 node failover without performance degradation
items.description: Cluster capacity planning must ensure that in an N-node cluster, the total memory and vCPU allocated to workloads does not exceed the remaining capacity of (N-1) nodes. A reserve of at least 32GB RAM per node should be dedicated exclusively to host OS and Storage Spaces Direct cache operations.

items.text: Cluster Validation tests have been executed with zero critical errors prior to production use
items.description: Execute failover cluster validation ('Test-Cluster' or the Azure Local Deployment Wizard verification) across all components (Inventory, Network, Storage Spaces Direct, System Configuration) and confirm all tests pass cleanly without errors before placing production workloads.

items.text: Dual power supplies are connected to independent Power Distribution Units (PDUs / UPS)
items.description: All cluster nodes must be equipped with redundant power supply units (PSUs) plugged into separate physical power feeds or independent uninterruptible power supplies (UPS / A+B feeds) to protect against facility power loss or breaker trips.

items.text: Generation 2 Virtual Machines with Virtual TPM (vTPM) and Secure Boot are deployed by default
items.description: Standardize all guest workloads on Generation 2 Hyper-V virtual machines. Gen 2 VMs provide UEFI boot, accelerated synthetic SCSI controllers, support for virtual TPM (vTPM), guest BitLocker, and eliminate legacy BIOS device emulation overhead.

items.text: All planned storage pools use direct-attached NVMe, SSD, or SAS drives in pass-through (IT) mode
items.description: Storage Spaces Direct requires raw direct-attached storage (SATA, SAS, or NVMe). Drives must be exposed directly to the operating system via a pure Host Bus Adapter (HBA) running in IT (Initiator Target) mode. Hardware RAID controllers or RAID caching must not be used on storage pool disks.

items.text: Disks are symmetrical in model, capacity, and firmware across all nodes
items.description: All nodes in the cluster must possess an identical drive layout (same quantity, type, capacity, and firmware per tier). Drive capacity imbalances across nodes lead to uneven pool utilization and degraded write performance.

items.text: Three-way mirroring is utilized for production workloads on clusters with 3 or more nodes
items.description: Three-way mirroring provides the highest performance and fault tolerance, tolerating simultaneous drive or node failures without downtime. Two-way mirroring is strictly reserved for 2-node clusters with a witness.

items.text: Mirror-accelerated parity is restricted to sequential, archive, or backup workloads
items.description: Parity and Mirror-Accelerated Parity (MAP) trade random write IOPS for capacity efficiency. High-performance, random-write workloads (like SQL databases, transaction logs, and VDI) must never be hosted on pure parity tiers.

items.text: Storage pool maintains reserve capacity equal to at least one capacity drive per node
items.description: Always maintain sufficient unallocated storage space in the storage pool to allow automated in-place repair and re-sync of volume data immediately following a disk failure, without requiring immediate technician physical drive replacement.

items.text: Delimited volume allocation is enabled on clusters with 4 or more nodes
items.description: Delimited allocation bounds volume data copies to a designated subset of nodes (e.g., 3 or 4 nodes out of an 8-node cluster). This prevents a multi-node failure from affecting all volumes simultaneously, dramatically increasing cluster survivability.

items.text: Cluster Shared Volumes (CSVs) are created in multiples of cluster node count and balanced
items.description: Create CSVs in integer multiples of the cluster node count (e.g., 2 CSVs per node in a 4-node cluster) and distribute volume ownership evenly across all nodes. This balances CSV metadata coordinator responsibilities and optimizes SMB Multichannel network bandwidth.

items.text: CSV in-memory read caching is enabled and appropriately sized
items.description: In-memory read caching allocates host RAM to accelerate unbuffered read operations. Configure CSV cache (typically 1GB to 4GB per host for standard workloads; up to larger sizes for VDI) using 'BlockCacheSize' parameter.

items.text: Volumes are formatted with ReFS using 64KB allocation unit size
items.description: All Cluster Shared Volumes must be formatted with the Resilient File System (ReFS) using a 64KB cluster allocation size. ReFS delivers near-instant VHDX creation, accelerated checkpoint merging (block cloning), real-time metadata repair, and sparse volume support.

items.text: DiskSpd or VMFleet baselining has been conducted prior to production workload onboarding
items.description: Execute synthetic stress and baseline testing using DiskSpd or VMFleet across all nodes prior to migrating production workloads. Establish baseline read/write IOPS, 99th percentile latencies, and verify failover behavior under simulated load.

items.text: Nested Resiliency (Nested 2-Way Mirror or Nested MAP) is evaluated for 2-node clusters
items.description: For 2-node clusters, consider Nested Two-Way Mirroring or Nested Mirror-Accelerated Parity. Unlike standard two-way mirroring which cannot tolerate a drive failure on the remaining node during node maintenance, nested resiliency allows survival of a drive failure even when one server is offline.

items.text: The ratio of capacity drives to cache drives is a uniform multiple across all nodes
items.description: When implementing hybrid storage pools (e.g., NVMe cache with SSD/HDD capacity), the number of capacity drives must be an integer multiple of the number of cache drives per node (e.g., 2 cache to 8 capacity drives = 4:1) to ensure even cache tier distribution.

items.text: No mixing of disparate drive bus protocols (NVMe, SAS, SATA) within the same tier
items.description: Ensure that within a given tier (cache or capacity), all drives utilize the same bus protocol and form factor. Mixing SAS and NVMe drives within the same capacity tier causes unpredictable queue depths and severe storage controller bottlenecks.

items.text: Storage pool repair task priority is calibrated to balance repair speed and tenant I/O
items.description: Review the Storage Spaces Direct repair task priority ('Set-StoragePool -RepairPolicy'). Balance automatic data re-sync speed after disk replacement against production VM latency requirements to avoid degraded tenant performance during rebuilds.

items.text: Host networking configuration is declared and enforced using Network ATC
items.description: Deploy host virtual switches, teaming, VLANs, and adapter properties using Network ATC intents ('Add-NetIntent'). Network ATC enforces standard Microsoft-tested network configurations, prevents configuration drift, and dynamically repairs deviations.

items.text: Physical network adapters are redundant and symmetrically connected to independent ToR switches
items.description: Every cluster node must have redundant network adapters (minimum 25GbE recommended for S2D) connected to independent top-of-rack (ToR) physical switches configured with MLAG, vPC, or independent subnets to prevent any single point of failure.

items.text: RDMA (RoCEv2 or iWARP) is enabled and validated on all storage adapters
items.description: Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) must be enabled on storage adapters to provide high throughput, sub-millisecond latency, and bypass host CPU overhead for Storage Spaces Direct SMB traffic. Validate functionality using 'Test-RDMA.ps1'.

items.text: Priority Flow Control (PFC) and Enhanced Transmission Selection (ETS) are configured on switches for RoCEv2
items.description: When using RoCEv2, configure Lossless Ethernet with PFC (Priority 3) and ETS (minimum 50% reserved bandwidth) across both physical switches and host adapters. Mismatches between switch DCB configurations and host settings cause packet drops and severe storage pauses.

items.text: Jumbo Frames (MTU 9014 or 9216) are enabled end-to-end along the storage path
items.description: Configure Jumbo Frames (MTU 9014 on host adapters and MTU 9216 on physical switches) across all storage networks. Jumbo frames reduce packet processing overhead, improve CPU efficiency, and maximize RDMA line-rate throughput.

items.text: Storage adapters are on non-routable subnets with NO default gateways configured
items.description: Each storage network adapter must be assigned a static IP on an isolated, non-routable VLAN/subnet (Storage 1 and Storage 2). Storage adapters must NEVER have a default gateway configured, preventing SMB storage traffic from attempting to route through external firewalls.

items.text: Clusters with 4 or more nodes use switched storage networking rather than switchless
items.description: While 2-node and 3-node clusters support switchless direct-connect interconnects, clusters with 4 or more nodes must use switched storage networking with redundant ToR switches to prevent excessive cabling complexity and ensure predictable bandwidth.

items.text: Network HUD (Heads-Up Display) is active and monitoring adapter health
items.description: Network HUD continuously analyzes adapter drivers, PCIe flappings, and physical link errors, automatically diagnosing and surfacing actionable hardware issues before they degrade cluster stability.

items.text: SDN deployments include at least 3 Network Controller VMs and regular state backups
items.description: When deploying Software Defined Networking (SDN) for microsegmentation or virtual networks, deploy a minimum of 3 Network Controller VMs distributed across distinct physical nodes and configure automated backups of the Network Controller database.

items.text: Dual-link full mesh interconnect cabling is implemented on 2-node and 3-node switchless clusters
items.description: For switchless cluster topologies, ensure redundant dual-link direct cabling exists between every node pair (full mesh). Redundant interconnect links ensure a single failed cable or NIC port does not sever inter-node communication.

items.text: Minimum bandwidth reservation is configured when sharing virtual switches for Compute and Management
items.description: If management and tenant compute traffic share converged physical network adapters, configure minimum bandwidth reservations (Weight or Absolute) via Network ATC or Hyper-V QoS to prevent runaway tenant traffic from starving management and cluster heartbeats.

items.text: Live Migration network order is prioritized to use RDMA storage networks
items.description: Configure the cluster Live Migration network priority order to select SMB/RDMA storage interfaces first. Live Migration over RDMA dramatically accelerates VM evacuation during host maintenance while keeping CPU overhead near zero.

items.text: Proxy configuration includes static bypass rules for local subnets and link-local ranges
items.description: When an outbound HTTP proxy is configured for Azure Local registration and updates ('Set-AzStackHciRegistrationProxy'), ensure the proxy bypass list explicitly contains all local cluster subnets, management IPs, and 169.254.0.0/16 link-local addresses.

items.text: Redundant DNS servers are configured with static forward and reverse lookup records
items.description: All cluster nodes must be configured with at least two highly available DNS servers. Verify forward (A) and reverse (PTR) DNS records exist for all node management adapters, cluster name object (CNO), and the Arc Resource Bridge IP.

items.text: Azure Arc Resource Bridge (ARB) is deployed and healthy on the cluster
items.description: The Azure Arc Resource Bridge appliance VM enables Azure Resource Manager control-plane operations on-premises. Verify the ARB appliance is in 'Running' state, has sufficient resources, and connectivity to Azure Arc control plane.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.resourceconnector/appliances' | project id, name, properties.status, location

items.text: Custom Location is properly configured and mapped to the Azure Local cluster
items.description: Ensure a Custom Location resource exists in Azure mapped to the Arc Resource Bridge and Azure Local cluster. This serves as the target deployment construct for Arc VMs, Logical Networks, and Storage Paths.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.extendedlocation/customlocations' | project id, name, location, properties

items.text: Logical Networks and Storage Paths are defined for native Arc VM provisioning
items.description: Configure Logical Networks (with static IP pools or DHCP) and Storage Paths in Azure to enable self-service VM lifecycle management (create, resize, start, stop, snapshot) from Azure Portal, ARM, Bicep, or Terraform.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.azurestackhci/logicalnetworks' or type =~ 'microsoft.azurestackhci/storagecontainers' | project id, name, type, location

items.text: Virtual machines are managed natively through Azure Arc VM control plane
items.description: Leverage Azure Arc VM management to automate VM operations, attach Azure tags, enforce Azure Policy guest configurations, and apply VM extensions (such as Azure Monitor Agent and Azure Connected Machine Agent) from the cloud.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.azurestackhci/virtualmachineinstances' | project id, name, properties.status, location

items.text: Required Azure Arc outbound firewall endpoints are whitelisted without SSL termination
items.description: Cluster nodes and the Arc Resource Bridge must have uninterrupted outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) connectivity to required Azure endpoints. Network firewalls and proxies must NOT perform SSL inspection / TLS interception on Azure Arc endpoints, which breaks certificate pinning.

items.text: Service Principal / Managed Identity credentials for Arc registration follow least privilege
items.description: Use dedicated Microsoft Entra service principals with scoped RBAC roles ('Azure Connected Machine Onboarding', 'Azure Stack HCI Administrator') for cluster registration. Ensure automated secret rotation or Managed Identity is implemented.

items.text: Edge clusters are registered to Azure Arc Fleet Management for multi-cluster governance
items.description: For organizations deploying multiple Azure Local clusters across branch offices or edge locations, organize clusters into centralized resource groups and Azure Arc Fleet structures for unified policy enforcement, compliance tracking, and update orchestration.

items.text: Azure Local cluster maintains regular cloud sync (at least once every 30 days)
items.description: Verify the cluster syncs with Azure at least once every 30 days to validate licensing and subscription status. If disconnected beyond 30 days, the cluster enters an out-of-policy state that restricts creating new virtual machines.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.azurestackhci/clusters' | project id, name, properties.status, properties.registrationTimestamp, properties.lastSyncTimestamp

items.text: Azure Arc VM and Host extensions are configured with automatic upgrade enabled
items.description: Enable automatic upgrade for installed Azure Arc extensions (Azure Monitor Agent, Azure Connected Machine Agent, Telemetry extension) to guarantee continuous patch compliance without manual intervention.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines/extensions' | project id, name, properties.type, properties.autoUpgradeMinorVersion

items.text: Azure Local Security Baseline is enabled and enforced across all nodes
items.description: Enforce the built-in Azure Local security baseline (default in 23H2/24H2), which automatically hardens over 300 OS and hypervisor security settings, disallows legacy protocols (SMBv1, TLS 1.0/1.1), and enforces secure cipher suites.

items.text: Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) is active in Enforced mode
items.description: Ensure WDAC is operating in enforced mode across all cluster nodes to restrict executable binaries, drivers, and PowerShell scripts strictly to trusted Microsoft and certified hardware partner signatures, mitigating zero-day malware execution.

items.text: BitLocker volume encryption is enabled on all Cluster Shared Volumes and OS drives
items.description: Enable BitLocker encryption on all CSV volumes and host OS drives backed by TPM 2.0 protectors. BitLocker safeguards data-at-rest against physical disk theft or unauthorized hardware removal from edge facilities.

items.text: Windows Defender Credential Guard is enabled on all cluster nodes
items.description: Credential Guard isolates secrets (such as NTLM password hashes and Kerberos tickets) inside a virtualization-based security enclaved memory container, preventing Pass-the-Hash and Pass-the-Ticket credential theft attacks.

items.text: SMB encryption and SMB signing are enforced for intra-cluster traffic
items.description: Configure SMB encryption for inter-node Storage Spaces Direct and live migration communications to protect cluster data in-transit across physical network switches from sniffing or tampering.

items.text: Active Directory Group Policy inheritance is blocked on the Azure Local cluster OU
items.description: Cluster computer accounts must reside in a dedicated Organizational Unit (OU) with GPO inheritance blocked. Misconfigured domain-wide Group Policies (such as User Rights Assignment, firewall, or audit overrides) can break cluster services and Hyper-V virtualization.

items.text: Just-Enough-Administration (JEA), LAPS, and PIM are used for host administrative access
items.description: Avoid persistent domain administrator logins to host servers. Use Windows LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution) for unique local admin passwords, Just-Enough-Administration (JEA) endpoints for maintenance, and Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for Azure RBAC roles.

items.text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Defender for Endpoint are active across nodes
items.description: Integrate Azure Local cluster hosts with Microsoft Defender for Cloud (Defender for Servers) to ensure continuous threat detection, anti-malware real-time protection, and compliance vulnerability scanning.

items.text: Deployment credentials used during cluster orchestration are revoked or deactivated
items.description: Temporary administrative accounts created solely to run initial Active Directory prep or cloud deployment scripts should have credentials rotated, permissions revoked, or accounts disabled post-commissioning.

items.text: Cluster updates are executed via Azure Local Lifecycle Manager / Azure Update Manager
items.description: Utilize Azure Local Lifecycle Manager (LCM) to apply full-stack, orchestrated, one-click updates encompassing host OS patches, OEM hardware firmware, BIOS, drivers, and Arc infrastructure agents with automated node draining and zero workload disruption.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.azurestackhci/updates' or type =~ 'microsoft.azurestackhci/updateruns' | project id, name, properties

items.text: Cluster-Aware Updating (CAU) node drain and live migration behavior is validated
items.description: Verify that during automated or manual update sequences, nodes enter maintenance mode, migrate tenant VMs seamlessly to healthy partner nodes, update and reboot cleanly, and safely resume without dropping VM connectivity.

items.text: Environment Checker and Hardware Validation tests run before updates or major changes
items.description: Run 'Invoke-AzStackHciConnectivityChecker' and 'Test-AzStackHciHardwareValidation' to verify network connectivity, DNS resolution, time synchronization (NTP), certificates, and storage health prior to applying update rings or major changes.

items.text: Azure Local Insights is configured with Azure Monitor Agent and Log Analytics workspace
items.description: Deploy Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) and configure Data Collection Rules (DCR) pointing to a centralized Log Analytics workspace. Enable Azure Local Insights to visualize cluster CPU, memory, storage pool capacity, IOPS, and latency across all nodes.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.insights/datacollectionrules' or type =~ 'microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces' | project id, name, location

items.text: Azure Monitor metric and log alert rules are configured for critical cluster fault conditions
items.description: Set up automated Azure Monitor alerts for node unexpected disconnect, storage pool available capacity dropping below 15%, physical drive faults, cluster quorum degradation, and Arc Resource Bridge heartbeat failure.

items.text: Cluster Health Service is operational with no unresolved critical faults
items.description: Verify via 'Get-HealthFault' in PowerShell or Azure Portal that the Cluster Health Service reports zero active critical hardware, storage, or network faults. Ensure fault notifications are wired to operational ticketing systems.

items.text: Authoritative NTP / PTP time synchronization is configured on all hosts and domain controllers
items.description: Ensure all nodes synchronize with reliable, authoritative NTP time sources. Inconsistent clock skew between nodes breaks Kerberos authentication, cluster heartbeats, Storage Spaces Direct metadata sequencing, and Arc token generation.

items.text: Cluster configuration and VM deployments are codified using ARM, Bicep, or Terraform
items.description: Maintain version-controlled declarative templates (Bicep, ARM, or Terraform) for all Azure Local resource definitions (Logical Networks, Storage Containers, Virtual Machines, Arc Extensions). Codification prevents manual configuration drift and enables automated recovery.

items.text: Windows Admin Center (WAC) is deployed in gateway mode and updated with latest extensions
items.description: Deploy Windows Admin Center on a dedicated gateway server with HTTPS certificates and keep Azure Stack HCI / Azure Local extensions updated to enable local GUI troubleshooting when external cloud access is impaired.

items.text: AKS enabled by Azure Arc is deployed following reference networking and storage architectures
items.description: Deploy Arc-enabled AKS worker clusters with dedicated container subnets (Calico or Azure CNI) and Container Storage Interface (CSI) storage classes backed by high-performance CSVs.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.kubernetes/connectedclusters' | project id, name, location, properties.agentVersion

items.text: GitOps and Flux v2 extensions are leveraged for automated Kubernetes workload deployment
items.description: Utilize Azure Arc GitOps (Flux v2) configuration extensions to manage Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, and cluster configurations declaratively from Git repositories rather than ad-hoc kubectl access.

items.text: Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) for Azure Local is implemented for low-latency or sovereign VDI
items.description: Deploy Windows 10/11 Enterprise multi-session host pools on Azure Local to satisfy data residency, local peripheral, or sub-millisecond edge latency requirements, leveraging existing cloud AVD management control plane.

items.text: SQL Server workloads leverage separate CSVs for data, log, and tempdb files
items.description: For high-performance SQL Server or database VMs on Azure Local, separate Data files (.mdf), Transaction Log files (.ldf), and TempDB across distinct Cluster Shared Volumes with dedicated formatting and cache considerations.

items.text: Azure Arc-enabled Data Services (SQL Managed Instance) evaluated for cloud-native edge database needs
items.description: Evaluate Azure Arc-enabled SQL Managed Instance on AKS on Azure Local for cloud-like automated patching, built-in high availability, elastic scaling, and unified Azure billing for on-premises database instances.

items.text: Application-consistent VM backup solution is configured and routinely tested
items.description: Configure VM backups using Microsoft Azure Backup Server (MABS), Microsoft Data Protection Manager (DPM), or certified partner solutions (Veeam, Commvault) leveraging VSS Hyper-V integration for application consistency. Regularly test restore drills.

items.text: Azure Site Recovery (ASR) is configured for critical workload replication to Azure or a secondary cluster
items.description: Protect business-critical Hyper-V VMs using Azure Site Recovery to orchestrate continuous replication, automated failover, and non-disruptive disaster recovery testing.

items.text: Stretch clustering synchronous replication satisfies network latency requirements (sub-5ms RTT)
items.description: For multi-site stretch clusters with synchronous Storage Replica, verify round-trip network latency between sites remains consistently below 5 milliseconds with sufficient dedicated bandwidth for replication.

items.text: Replication networks are isolated from management and VM traffic in stretch cluster designs
items.description: Storage Replica traffic requires dedicated, redundant network interfaces and isolated VLANs separate from cluster management, tenant compute, and local Storage Spaces Direct traffic.

items.text: Quorum witness is located in a neutral third site (Cloud Witness in Azure)
items.description: When deploying a 2-site stretch cluster, the quorum witness must reside in a separate independent third site (such as Azure Cloud Witness) to ensure automatic, split-brain-free failover when either physical facility goes down.

items.text: Site recovery and manual failover procedures are documented and validated
items.description: Document an operational runbook detailing steps for catastrophic site failure, manual quorum override ('Start-ClusterNode -FixQuorum'), forced volume mount, and subsequent recovery synchronization.

items.text: Storage backing log volumes is equal to or faster than data volumes in stretch clusters
items.description: Storage Replica log volumes record write operations synchronously before sending acknowledgements. Place log volumes on high-speed NVMe or fast flash storage to prevent log write bottlenecks from slowing down application I/O.

items.text: Recovery Point Objective (RPO) and Recovery Time Objective (RTO) are documented and verified
items.description: Establish formal RPO and RTO SLA metrics for each application tier hosted on Azure Local. Match synchronous replication (RPO=0) to tier-1 systems and asynchronous replication or backup snapshots to tier-2/3 systems.

items.text: Azure Hybrid Benefit (AHB) for Windows Server is applied to waive host service fees
items.description: Apply Azure Hybrid Benefit for Windows Server Datacenter with active Software Assurance (SA). AHB waives the monthly Azure Local host fee per physical core and grants rights to run unlimited Windows Server guest VMs on the cluster.

items.text: Cluster registration is associated with the appropriate enterprise subscription and tags
items.description: Ensure the Azure Local cluster is registered under the correct billing subscription and enriched with mandatory enterprise governance tags (CostCenter, Environment, Owner, Application, Location) for transparent cost allocation.
items.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.azurestackhci/clusters' | project id, name, subscriptionId, tags

items.text: Virtual machine resource allocation is monitored and right-sized to prevent CPU/RAM waste
items.description: Regularly audit VM CPU and memory consumption using Azure Local Insights. Right-size over-provisioned VMs and avoid unmonitored dynamic memory ballooning on mission-critical database hosts.

items.text: Data deduplication and compression are evaluated on secondary and archive volumes
items.description: Enable ReFS deduplication and compression on general-purpose file servers, VDI user profile disks, or backup repository volumes to maximize storage efficiency and lower raw storage footprint costs.

items.text: Static memory sizing is configured for transactional databases to avoid overcommit penalties
items.description: Avoid configuring Dynamic Memory on latency-sensitive transactional databases (like SQL Server or Oracle). Static memory assignment guarantees predictable memory paging performance and eliminates hypervisor ballooning overhead.

metadata.description: Comprehensive review checklist for Azure Local (formerly Azure Stack HCI) deployments, aligning with Microsoft Well-Architected Framework and production engineering standards.
